ATTACHED MANUEL ACADEMY LEARNER RESOURCE

Resource ID: ma-resource:ma-g7-arts-and-music-u02-l06

Lesson focus: design iteration

Resource type: ACADEMY_CREATED_SCAFFOLD

GUIDED SCAFFOLD B — support-fading pass for design iteration. Earlier-pass substitute: Two wayfinding drafts can use the same words but different hierarchy; a five-second find test reveals which supports the stated route. Mark the relationship involving purpose as the fragile move, then hide this resource. Make two new studies, loops, maps, or responses without the prompt. Reopen only afterward; compare the order of decisions and the evidence. Report whether the fragile move held. If it did not, use the criteria to name the mismatch without changing the learner’s intent or copying the example. Use it to study design iteration; describe evidence before judging and adapt the demonstrated relationship rather than copying a finished work.

How to use it: Use the attached earlier-pass substitute when prior work is unavailable, hide it as directed, and finish both unassisted studies before checking.

Rights: Manuel Academy original; licensed CC BY 4.0 for learner use and adaptation. No third-party text, image, score, lyric, melody, recording, or performance is included.

Access and materials: Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
critique_criteria: The submission contains the required work blocks and one reviewable process state; each required artifact, study, response, or process note can be located.
The learner locates relevant purpose, audience need, hierarchy, legibility, constraints, feedback, and iteration and explains how the evidence relates to the stated intent, claim, or criterion.
The learner states an intent or claim and supports it with observable evidence while retaining ownership of artistic decisions.
The process record shows a check and a learner-chosen revision or reasoned decision to keep the result.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available for spoken reflection, explanation, or critique and scores the same. Use a labelled visual, tactile, constructed, or accessible digital work to preserve the making target; prose alone does not claim visual or material technique evidence. You may describe the work in writing and have one trusted adult verify a physical artifact without photographing you or your home. No microphone, camera, or recording is required.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Provide a non-performance or low-audience option when needed without lowering the academic target.

media.fallback: Use the complete adjacent verbal description and recreate the relationships with raised or movable paper forms. The required Academy model is attached; no outside search is needed.

remediation: Route 1: Reduce design iteration to three locatable events, areas, steps, or decisions. Label the intended effect beside each and underline the one purpose relationship that should carry it. Use a separate small study, four-event loop, thumbnail, evidence table, or paper plan. The adult may model the noticing process on different material but may not change the learner’s work. Check yourself: Point to or name the exact purpose evidence before deciding whether it serves the intent. New attempt: Put the support away and make a new arrangement, passage, response, or plan; record what the new evidence shows. Route 2: Return to the last understandable state. Hold every relationship steady except one chosen feature from purpose, audience need, hierarchy, legibility, constraints, feedback, and iteration; predict what that single change should do. Test the feature on scrap paper, a silent count, a two-event rehearsal loop, movable shapes, or a short evidence sentence before changing the scored work. Check yourself: Name what stayed the same, what changed, and the first observable result—without using “better” as the evidence. New attempt: Create a different small case using the same one-variable method, then transfer the finding to the original task only if it serves the learner’s intent.
extension: Apply design iteration under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on design iteration rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.

concept_instruction.title: What design iteration means here
concept_instruction.body: Design organizes choices to serve a stated purpose under real constraints.

concept_instruction.title: How the relationship changes the result
concept_instruction.body: A brief turns a need into testable criteria; contrasting sketches expose tradeoffs before time is spent refining one direction.

concept_instruction.title: Choice and tradeoff
concept_instruction.body: A solution can maximize speed, clarity, expression, access, or cost, but rarely all at once. A strong rationale names what was prioritized and why. Worked example: Two wayfinding drafts can use the same words but different hierarchy; a five-second find test reveals which supports the stated route. Non-example: Choosing the most polished draft without checking it against the brief treats taste as evidence.

technique_sequence.action: State the intended effect or question before making or judging.
technique_sequence.notice: The statement creates a criterion that can be checked.
technique_sequence.why: Arts evidence is interpreted in relation to purpose, not personal taste.

technique_sequence.action: Identify or set up the relevant purpose, audience need, hierarchy, legibility, constraints, feedback, and iteration.
technique_sequence.notice: Locate the first relationship that can be observed in design iteration.
technique_sequence.why: A brief turns a need into testable criteria; contrasting sketches expose tradeoffs before time is spent refining one direction.

technique_sequence.action: Complete one small controlled study or rehearsal loop.
technique_sequence.notice: Keep most relationships stable so one decision remains readable.
technique_sequence.why: A bounded test makes cause and effect easier to notice.

technique_sequence.action: Transfer the idea to a fresh work, excerpt, source detail, or project decision.
technique_sequence.notice: Close the model or cue before the independent decision.

technique_sequence.action: Check against criteria and choose a revision or a reasoned decision to keep the result.
technique_sequence.notice: Cite a location, moment, event, or process fact before judging.
technique_sequence.why: Evidence protects creative variation and learner authority.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: The stated intent for design iteration is present, but the record does not yet locate purpose, audience need, hierarchy, legibility, constraints, feedback, and iteration that supports it.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The learner supports a different, ambiguous, subtle, or intentionally open effect with observable evidence.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: Several relationships changed at once, so the learner cannot yet tell which choice caused the observed effect.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The task is an intentionally exploratory diagnostic and no causal claim is being scored.
